truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 contained 12 true vulnerabilities fully and 2 partially, and missed 6 true vulnerabilities. It also overclaimed severity or CWE on several found items. No unsupported false-positive findings were admitted beyond the overclaims listed.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: If runtime_log_format is attacker-controlled through a config file, printf format specifiers such as %n can cause memory reads/writes or other undefined behavior.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the runtime log format format-string issue and linked it to config log_format. It under-ran severity but contained the vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Expressions such as fact(large integer) can cause a long or hanging loop and signed overflow of the long long result.
Items.Notes: The audited answer identified the fact() signed overflow but framed it primarily as DoS/resource exhaustion with CWE-400 and Medium severity, rather than the true High CWE-190 integer overflow.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Worker threads may dereference scratch after the global memory pool has freed it during cleanup, causing memory corruption, crashes, or code execution.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the deferred history flush scratch buffer being used after memory pool cleanup.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Malicious validator_path or config_file values from a config file can inject shell commands when admin validate is run.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified config validation command injection. It under-ran severity but contained the vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: An expression with std::string length >= 1024 reaches strcpy into input_buffer_[1024], causing an out-of-bounds stack write and possible control-flow corruption.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the inverted length check leading to strcpy into the stack buffer. It overclaimed severity as Critical and used CWE-787 instead of the truth CWE-120/CWE-121.
The audited answer did not identify the ThreadSafeCounter race where old_value is read before acquiring the lock and then written back under the lock.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: After five failed attempts, any input containing EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE grants administrative access without a valid credential.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the emergency override logic bomb. It overclaimed severity as Critical and used CWE-287 instead of the truth CWE-511.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: An authenticated admin can load arbitrary files by supplying traversal sequences, allowing attacker-chosen settings such as log_format or validator_path to be applied.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified config filename path traversal. It overclaimed severity as High versus the truth Medium.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: A long expression parsed in the background can overflow the 256-byte expression_buffer_, corrupting the memory pool and potentially enabling code execution.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the 256-byte expression buffer unchecked strcpy heap overflow. The CWE label was less precise, but the vulnerability was present.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Anyone with source access or binary string extraction can use the admin password to authenticate.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the hardcoded administrator secret.
The audited answer did not identify the weak PRNG-based 4-digit session token generation.
The audited answer did not identify the thread-unsafe static tm cached_time / localtime race in logging.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: If TMPDIR or TEMP is attacker-controlled, path contents can inject shell commands into the system() call.
Items.Notes: The audited answer identified the same unsafe temporary path and system() construction, but classified it as shell command injection rather than insecure temporary file handling.
The audited answer did not identify persistent authentication state as a distinct weakness involving authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: A non-numeric or out-of-range third variable token throws std::invalid_argument or std::out_of_range, which is not caught locally and causes main to exit.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the unhandled std::stod in variable parsing. The CWE label was less precise, but the vulnerability was present.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: When previous_size is only slightly larger than size, remaining underflows to a huge value and fragment.data points outside the allocated block, enabling later out-of-bounds reads/writes and heap corruption.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the MemoryPool split integer underflow.
The audited answer did not identify unbounded recursion through parse_expression / parse_factor on nested parentheses.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Concurrent background expression analysis can read/write the same unordered_map without locking, leading to crashes or memory corruption.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified the result cache data race.
The audited answer did not identify the TOCTOU window between filesystem::exists and opening the config file after sleep_for.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: An empty or whitespace-only input line causes integer division by zero, terminating the program via undefined behavior or a floating-point exception.
Items.Notes: The audited answer explicitly identified integer division by zero in calculate_route_score.
